title: Recording: Hey Baby, You Don’t Know Me At All, Spooky Weirdness by Ringo Starr | 1976
content:
Cherokee Studios, Los Angeles
Producer: Arif Mardin

Ringo Starr recorded three songs for his fifth studio album, Ringo’s Rotogravure, on 4 June 1976.

‘Hey Baby’ was originally recorded by Bruce Channel in 1961, and became the second single released from Starr’s album.

I think Arif Mardin who was producing that album made the call about covering the old Bruce Channel hit. Arif had a difficult time with me because I was difficult at that period of my life. He and Ahmet were two of the best people in the music business ever. Arif was such a gentle man and there are not enough of them in the world. I can’t really even tell you if it was a great experience because a lot of it is… gone. The proof is we’ve got the record – and that’s about it.
Ringo Starr
Photograph – The Very Best Of Ringo Starr

‘You Don’t Know Me At All’ was written by New Zealand songwriter Dave Jordan, an in-house writer-producer at Chappell Music who wrote for artists including Roger Whittaker, Sasha Distel, and Demis Roussos as well as releasing solo albums.

It was released as a single in Europe on 15 October 1976, with ‘Cryin” on the b-side. The single featured additional overdubs missing from the album mix.

The day’s final recording, ‘Spooky Weirdness’, closed the album. It was an ad-libbed experimental piece lasting under 90 seconds, something of a throwaway space-filler at the close of the album.
